questions.q: What must the people of Israel do when they possess the land which Yahweh has given them?
questions.a: The people of Israel must take some of the first of all the harvest of the land in a basket and go to the place Yahweh has chosen for them to worship.

questions.q: What must they say to the priest when they give him the basket?
questions.a: They must tell the priest that they declare to Yahweh that they have come and settled in the land that he swore to give to their ancestors.

questions.q: What must they say about their ancestor?
questions.a: The people of Israel must say that their ancestor was a wandering Aramean.

questions.q: How did the Egyptians treat the Israelites when they were in Egypt?
questions.a: The Egyptians treated the Israelites badly and afflicted them, making them do the work of slaves.

questions.q: How did Yahweh bring Israel out of Egypt?
questions.a: He brought them out with a mighty hand, with a display of his great fearsome power, with signs, and with wonders.

questions.q: What is the purpose for setting down the basket before Yahweh?
questions.a: The purpose is to worship Yahweh and rejoice in all the good that he has done for Israel, their families, the Levites, and the foreigners among them.

questions.q: What must they do after they have finished giving all the tithe from their harvest?
questions.a: They must give it to the Levites, to the foreigners, to the orphans, and to the widows so they may eat and be filled.

questions.q: What do the people of Israel want Yahweh to do for them?
questions.a: The people of Israel want Yahweh to look down from heaven and bless them and the land which he has given to them.

questions.q: What is Yahweh commanding the people to do?
questions.a: He is commanding them to obey his statues and decrees with all their heart and soul.

questions.q: What have the people declared before Yahweh?
questions.a: They have declared that Yahweh is their God and that they will walk in his ways, keep his commandments, and listen to and obey all that he tells them to do.

questions.q: What has Yahweh declared to the people of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh has declared that Israel is his own possession and he will set them high above all the other nations in respect to praise, reputation, and honor so they will be a people that is set apart and holy to him.

commentary.text: The prayer after disposal of the third year's tithe.
The covenant between God and the people.

Verses 1–11 When God has made good his promises to us, he expects we should own it to the honour of his faithfulness. And our creature comforts are doubly sweet, when we see them flowing from the fountain of the promise. The person who offered his first-fruits, must remember and own the mean origin of that nation, of which he was a member. A Syrian ready to perish was my father. Jacob is here called a Syrian. Their nation in its infancy sojourned in Egypt as strangers, they served there as slaves. They were a poor, despised, oppressed people in Egypt; and though become rich and great, had no reason to be proud, secure, or forgetful of God. He must thankfully acknowledge God's great goodness to Israel. The comfort we have in our own enjoyments, should lead us to be thankful for our share in public peace and plenty; and with present mercies we should bless the Lord for the former mercies we remember, and the further mercies we expect and hope for. He must offer his basket of first-fruits. Whatever good thing God gives us, it is his will that we make the most comfortable use we can of it, tracing the streams to the Fountain of all consolation.

How should the earth yield its increase, or, if it does, what comfort can we take in it, unless therewith our God gives us his blessing? All this represented the covenant relation between a reconciled God and every true believer, and the privileges and duties belonging to it. We must be watchful, and show that according to the covenant of grace in Christ Jesus, the Lord is our God, and we are his people, waiting in his appointed way for the performance of his gracious promises.

Moses here enforces the precepts. They are God's laws, therefore thou shalt do them, to that end were they given thee; do them, and dispute them not; do them, and draw not back; do them, not carelessly and hypocritically, but with thy heart and soul, thy whole heart and thy whole soul. We forswear ourselves, and break the most sacred engagement, if, when we have taken the Lord to be our God, we do not make conscience of obeying his commands. We are elected to obedience, 1Pe 1:2; chosen that we should be holy, Eph 1:4; purified a peculiar people, that we might not only do good works, but be zealous in them, Tit 2:14. Holiness is true honour, and the only way to everlasting honour.
